sections.h2: Can I sell a house in Texas while a tenant lives in it?
sections.html:
Yes. A sale of the owner's interest does not remove the tenant, and the lease keeps running while the house changes hands. What changes is who the landlord is, and with that, who answers for the deposit and the lease.

Chapter 92 of the Property Code covers residential landlords and tenants (Sec. 92.002). It does not give a seller a way to clear a tenant out before closing. Any move to end the tenancy has to follow the lease and the eviction process in Chapter 24, which is why most sellers either sell with the tenant in place or negotiate a move out date.

sections.h2: Who is responsible for the security deposit after the sale?
sections.html:
The new owner. Sec. 92.105 says that when the owner's interest ends by sale or otherwise, the new owner is liable for deposits from the date title passes.

  • The new owner must hand the tenant a signed statement acknowledging the purchase and the exact dollar amount of the deposit.
  • The former owner stays liable for a deposit received during ownership until the new owner has received it or assumed the liability, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.
  • A lender that takes title by foreclosure is excluded from the rule.

In practice, a seller should transfer the deposit at closing and list it on the settlement statement, then get the buyer's signed acknowledgment in writing so the tenant's notice is ready on the day title passes. A tenant's claim to the deposit takes priority over the landlord's creditors, including a trustee in bankruptcy (Sec. 92.103(c)).

sections.h2: What happens to the lease and the rent?
sections.html:
The lease continues on its own terms. The State Law Library explains that a landlord cannot raise the rent before the lease term is up without the tenant's agreement, and that once the term ends there is no state limit on a raise.

A landlord also cannot raise rent in retaliation for repair requests, good faith complaints to a government agency, or tenant organizing (Sec. 92.331, as the library summarizes it). A buyer who plans to raise rent should wait for the end of the lease term, and should read the lease before signing the contract. If the lease is month to month, the buyer's options are different, so ask a Texas real estate attorney.

The lease copy rule also matters when paperwork changes hands. A landlord must give at least one complete copy of the signed lease to a tenant within three business days (Sec. 92.024), so a buyer should keep a copy of the lease and every amendment.

sections.h2: Can a seller show the house to buyers?
sections.html:
Only as far as the lease allows. According to the State Law Library, Texas has no state law regulating landlord entry, so the lease controls. The lease may require prior notice, and it may name prospective buyers as people who may enter.

If the lease is silent, the landlord may not have a right to enter without permission, apart from emergencies and repairs. Entering more often than necessary, at unreasonable times, or against the lease can breach the tenant's implied right to quiet enjoyment. Ask the tenant for a showing schedule in writing, and keep a record of the agreement.

sections.h2: What can a landlord not do to get the tenant out?
sections.html:
Self help is limited. Sec. 92.008 bars a landlord from interrupting utilities the tenant pays directly, or those the landlord furnishes as part of the tenancy, except for bona fide repairs, construction or an emergency. Sec. 92.0081 bars removing doors, windows, locks or the landlord's furnished appliances other than for bona fide repair, and bars keeping a tenant out except by judicial process or in narrow cases.

One such case is changing the lock of a tenant who is behind on rent. The landlord must then post a written notice on the tenant's front door saying where to get the new key 24 hours a day, and that the landlord must provide it at any hour even if no rent is paid.

A seller who wants possession for a buyer who intends to live there needs a lawful reason, such as nonrenewal at the end of the lease, or an agreement with the tenant.

sections.h2: How do notice to vacate and eviction work?
sections.html:
The Texas State Law Library outlines the process for a tenant who stays after a proper notice. Under Property Code Sec. 24.005, the landlord must give at least three days of written notice to vacate unless the lease sets a different period, delivered in person, inside the premises in an obvious place, by mail, or by email if the lease allows it.

Texas eviction timing after notice to vacate
StageTiming
Notice to vacateAt least 3 days unless the lease says otherwise
Suit filed in justice courtHearing no sooner than 10 days and no later than 21 days after filing
Service on the tenantAt least 4 days before trial
Appeal to county courtWithin 5 days of the judgment
Writ of possessionAvailable 6 days after final judgment, with 24 hours' notice before removal

A federal 30 day notice may apply to some covered properties. A tenant on a lease that ends after the closing date remains in place after the sale unless a lawful process ends the tenancy.

sections.h2: What should a seller do before listing a tenant occupied house?
sections.html:
Gather the records first, then decide whether the sale will be with the tenant in place or empty.

  • Collect the lease, amendments, deposit records (Sec. 92.106 requires a landlord to keep accurate deposit records) and rent ledger.
  • Write down the deposit amount and prepare the buyer's signed acknowledgment.
  • Decide how showings will work and ask for access in writing.
  • Pay or prorate property tax. Texas taxes attach as a lien each January 1.
  • Ask the county tax office and the appraisal district whether any exemption on the property will change after the sale.

A cash buyer who accepts the property with the tenant in place can close without waiting for the tenant to leave, which suits sellers who cannot get possession quickly.

faqs.q: Does the tenant have to leave when I sell the house?
faqs.a: No. The sale does not end the lease. The tenant stays under the lease terms, and the buyer steps in as landlord.

faqs.q: Who gets the security deposit when a rented house is sold?
faqs.a: The new owner is liable for it from the date title passes and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact amount. The seller stays liable until the buyer receives the deposit or assumes liability.

faqs.q: Can I enter the house to show it to a buyer?
faqs.a: Only as the lease allows. Texas has no statute on landlord entry, so check the lease for a notice requirement and any mention of prospective buyers. If it is silent, get the tenant's permission.

faqs.q: Can I raise the rent before the buyer closes?
faqs.a: Not during the lease term without the tenant's agreement. After the term ends there is no state cap, but a raise cannot be a retaliation for repair requests or complaints.

faqs.q: How long does an eviction take in Texas?
faqs.a: Notice to vacate is at least three days, and the justice court hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing. A writ of possession is available six days after final judgment, and an appeal must be filed within five days.
